_doc: cast_bible_v1 (2026-11-01, content_style v2.5). Fixed characters, injected VERBATIM into the plan and script prompts by tools\brief_gen.py (style v2.5). Never regenerated per episode: the plan only assigns POSITIONS (who argues which side of the crux) and one personal stake per guest. To change a character: copy to cast_bible_v2.json and add a templates\README.md changelog line; never edit this file in place. Speaker labels are the real names. All personal stories are invented and modest; the characters are fictional AI voices. Nobody is a clone of Thomas.

excluded.Elliot: OUT: his Drama 3 voice is monotone (pitch std ~2-2.7 semitones, Elliot_v2 fixed pace not pitch). No bible until a new reference passes.
excluded.Hugh: NOT USABLE: Hugh is never paired with Carter and Carter always hosts, so there is no setup in which he can appear. No bible; brief_gen rejects him.
excluded.Maya, Declan, Alice, Mary: BANNED: never use, even if a brief names them (use Clara or Isla instead).

rules.weights: pick_cast weights from the handover still apply: Frank low weight, Samuel 0.25. Frank and Marcus are US men like Carter: never cast both in one episode (three similar voices); prefer pairing each with a woman or a non-US accent.
rules.catchphrase_cap: Each signature phrase at most twice per episode. Quirks are seasoning, not the meal: at most one quirk moment per speaker per chapter.
rules.concession: Each guest concedes exactly once per episode, on a side point, with a reason, in their own words (see concedes_like). The crux is never conceded.
rules.talk_to_each_other: Every chapter has at least one exchange where the two guests talk to each other (tease, challenge, inside joke), not to Carter.

host.name: Carter
host.who: Ex-high-school physics teacher who now runs a small bike repair shop in Dayton, Ohio. Two teenagers. Learns by taking things apart.
host.lens: 'Does it work on a Tuesday?' He judges every idea by what it does to ordinary people on an ordinary day.
host.job: Asks the listener's 'dumb' question; forces concreteness ('Give me an example. A real one.'); keeps score of who is winning; gives his own view every few minutes and is sometimes wrong. Once per episode a guest corrects him and he takes it well.
host.voice: Short sentences. 'Wait, wait.' 'Hang on.' Admits confusion out loud. Self-deprecating. Never a speech over about 60 words. About 30% of the words.
host.running_life: Exactly one 'this week at the shop / at home' story per episode: setup, twist, payoff. Never as filler.
host.hates: Jargon, hand-waving, people who won't pick a side.

Clara.who: Built products at a big tech company for ten years, now runs a five-person design-and-software studio. Treats her mistakes as data.
Clara.expertise: Product building, shipping software, what users actually do, iteration, startups.
Clara.lens: 'What I've seen work.' Argues from practice: a project, a client, a launch that went wrong and what fixed it.
Clara.natural_side: Optimist: problems are design problems and can be fixed by building better.
Clara.voice: Fast, warm, amused; laughs at her own jokes. Signature: 'Okay, but here's the thing.' One specific number per chapter, from the notes only.
Clara.quirk: Talks about ideas in software versions ('that's a version-one argument').
Clara.concedes_like: With a grin: 'Fine. I oversold that.' Concedes when shown a real failure case.
Clara.stake_hint: Her studio's clients and her team's livelihoods ride on this technology working.

Lachlan.who: Former aviation incident investigator who has read hundreds of accident reports. Now consults on safety reviews.
Lachlan.expertise: Accident investigation, safety engineering, risk, base rates, incentives, how systems fail.
Lachlan.lens: 'How does this fail, and who pays?' Argues from failure cases, base rates and incentives.
Lachlan.natural_side: Sceptic: assume it breaks, design for the breakage.
Lachlan.voice: Slow, dry, deadpan. Short punches and understatement ('That went well.'). Says 'mate' at most twice per episode. Rarely raises his voice, so when he does it lands.
Lachlan.quirk: Keeps a mock 'ledger' of the other guest's predictions that did or didn't come true.
Lachlan.concedes_like: Grudgingly and specifically: 'That's a better spec. I'll give you that one.' Concedes when shown a working safeguard.
Lachlan.stake_hint: He has sat with families after crashes that a checklist would have prevented.

Isla.archetype: the moral philosopher with dirt under her nails
Isla.who: Trained as a moral philosopher in Glasgow, left academia, now teaches evening ethics classes for adults and volunteers on a hospice ward.
Isla.expertise: Ethics (virtue ethics, Kant, utilitarian arguments), meaning, dignity, care, what a practice does to the people inside it.
Isla.lens: 'What does it do to the person doing it?' Judges ideas by the character they build, not only the outcomes.
Isla.natural_side: Humanist: suspicious of anything that treats people as numbers, equally suspicious of easy outrage.
Isla.voice: A long, careful sentence, then a blunt one-liner that lands. Gentle teasing. Signature: 'Say that again, slower.'
Isla.quirk: Quotes her late gran's sayings (at most once per episode, invented and homely, never presented as a real source).
Isla.flaw: Can drift into abstraction; Carter has to drag her back to Tuesday.
Isla.concedes_like: Openly: 'No, you're right about that part, and it matters.' Concedes when shown that a rule actually protects vulnerable people.
Isla.stake_hint: She has watched dying patients be helped or diminished by systems.

Marcus.who: Former insurance actuary, now teaches behavioural economics at a state university. Sees prices and trade-offs everywhere.
Marcus.expertise: Economics, incentives, base rates, statistics, markets, regulation trade-offs, unintended consequences.
Marcus.lens: 'Follow the incentive.' Asks who is paid to want this outcome and what it costs compared with the alternative.
Marcus.natural_side: Pragmatist: neither hype nor panic, just costs, benefits and who bears them.
Marcus.voice: Dry, precise, slightly professorial, then undercuts himself. Signature: 'What's the base rate?'
Marcus.quirk: Puts a price tag on everything, including absurd things ('that argument is worth about four dollars').
Marcus.flaw: Treats everything as priceable; misses what people refuse to trade.
Marcus.concedes_like: Precisely: 'Okay, that doesn't price. I'll take the loss on that one.' Concedes when something can't be put on a spreadsheet.
Marcus.stake_hint: He spent years pricing risks that later turned into real claims.

Willa.who: Ran trust-and-safety and content moderation at two social media startups, quit, now works for a digital civil-liberties group.
Willa.expertise: Platforms, moderation, how tech companies make decisions in practice, privacy, online harms, policy.
Willa.lens: 'I've been in that meeting.' Knows how decisions really get made inside companies and distrusts the press release.
Willa.natural_side: Critic of corporate power, but allergic to sloppy regulation too.
Willa.voice: Quick, sardonic, specific. Short insider anecdotes. Signature: 'Here's what actually happens.'
Willa.quirk: Translates corporate jargon into plain English on the spot ('"alignment" means "don't get us sued"').
Willa.flaw: Cynical; assumes bad faith where it is often just incompetence.
Willa.concedes_like: Sharp but fair: 'Fine, that one's on the regulators, not the company.' Concedes when shown a rule backfired.
Willa.stake_hint: She reviewed the worst content on the internet for years and knows what it does to moderators.

Zara.who: Historian of science and technology at a Cape Town university; writes about how societies absorbed the printing press, the telegraph, radio and the pill.
Zara.expertise: History of technology and science, colonial history, moral panics, how institutions adapt.
Zara.lens: 'We have been here before, and here is where the parallel breaks.' Brings one historical parallel per chapter, then tests it.
Zara.natural_side: Calm contextualiser: distrusts both 'this changes everything' and 'nothing new here'.
Zara.voice: Unhurried, warm authority; storytelling; dry irony. Signature: 'Let me take you back a bit.'
Zara.quirk: Names who got left out of every past revolution.
Zara.flaw: Can make everything sound like it has happened before.
Zara.concedes_like: Gracefully: 'That's where my parallel breaks. Scale is new.' Concedes when the history genuinely doesn't fit.
Zara.stake_hint: Her own family history runs through who got access to new technology and who didn't.

Imogen.who: Experimental psychologist / cognitive neuroscientist who runs a small lab and reviews papers for journals.
Imogen.expertise: Psychology, cognition, how studies work, replication, measurement, human bias.
Imogen.lens: 'What did they actually measure?' Separates what a study showed from what the headline said.
Imogen.natural_side: Sceptic of confident claims on both sides; follows the best evidence wherever it goes.
Imogen.voice: Precise, brisk, deadly understatement ('That's... ambitious.'). Signature: 'Small sample, big claim.'
Imogen.quirk: Grades claims out of five on the spot ('that's a two out of five').
Imogen.flaw: Discounts lived experience that hasn't been measured.
Imogen.concedes_like: Crisply: 'Fair. The lab doesn't capture that.' Concedes when lived experience reveals something the data misses.
Imogen.stake_hint: She has seen her own field's famous results fail to replicate.

Frank.who: Retired union electrician, now on his small town's city council. Wired factories, hospitals and data centres for forty years.
Frank.expertise: Work, trades, unions, local government, infrastructure, what changes mean for jobs and towns.
Frank.lens: 'Who cleans it up?' Judges ideas by what they do to workers, towns and the people left holding the bill.
Frank.natural_side: Common-sense populist: distrusts hype and distant experts, respects things that are built to last.
Frank.voice: Slow, plain, story-first; job-site anecdotes; folksy but sharp. Signature: 'I've pulled that wire.'
Frank.quirk: Measures everything against the safety code ('there's a code for that, written in somebody's blood').
Frank.flaw: Suspicious of anything new until it has a decade of track record.
Frank.concedes_like: Plainly: 'Alright. You got me there, and I don't like it.' Concedes when the numbers are concrete.
Frank.stake_hint: His town lost a plant once; he knows what a 'transition' feels like on the ground.

Samuel.archetype: the scale engineer from the Global South
Samuel.who: Software architect in Bengaluru who has built public-scale payment and identity systems used by hundreds of millions of people.
Samuel.expertise: Large-scale systems, digital public infrastructure, engineering trade-offs, the Global South view on technology.
Samuel.lens: 'At a billion users, rare is daily.' Thinks in scale, defaults and who is excluded by design.
Samuel.natural_side: Pragmatic builder who distrusts Silicon Valley's assumptions about who the users are.
Samuel.voice: Energetic, generous, funny, with quick numbers and analogies. Signature: 'Let me tell you what happens at scale.'
Samuel.quirk: Gently points out when a 'universal' argument only fits rich countries.
Samuel.flaw: Can treat individual harm as an acceptable edge case.
Samuel.concedes_like: Warmly: 'Okay, okay, that edge case is a person. I accept that.' Concedes on individual rights.
Samuel.stake_hint: His systems decide whether people's pensions arrive.

pairings._doc: Any two guests can work because each has a distinct lens; these are the strongest clashes. The plan uses the matching 'clash' line to set the crux. With ONE guest, Carter takes the opposite position himself.

best.clash: Build it vs. how does it fail. Old sparring partners; she calls him 'the human incident report', he keeps the ledger of her predictions.
Builder vs. insider critic: both from tech, opposite conclusions. Willa: 'I've been in that meeting.' Clara: 'I've run that meeting.'
Dignity vs. price tags: what cannot be traded vs. everything has a cost.
History of who was left out vs. scale engineering that includes or excludes by default; both reject the Silicon Valley frame, from opposite sides.
What can be measured vs. what matters but can't be measured.
Design for the crash vs. at scale you must accept some failure; both engineers, very different risk appetite.
The worker who cleans up vs. the builder who ships; Frank's code 'written in blood' vs. Clara's 'iterate'.
Corporate bad faith vs. incentives explain it without villains.
Long-view narrative vs. 'show me the data'; she tells the story, Imogen grades it.
Character and care vs. checklists and safeguards; both cautious, about different things.

avoid.why: Two US men next to US-male Carter: voices too similar for listeners.
Frank solo with Carter: same accent and similar register; prefer a two-guest episode with a woman or a non-US accent.

pairings.default_rule: If a pair is not listed: give the advocate side to the guest whose natural_side fits the topic's optimistic case and the attack to the other; make the crux the point where their lenses collide.

banned_phrases: hit the nail on the head
at the end of the day
